paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers met at the bus stop at half past eight. They came early, so they sat and waited for Teacher Kim. Then they took the bus to the shopping street in the town. The bus was almost empty, and they all found seats. Mia was very happy, because her dad's bike shop was on that street.

First, the club walked slowly along the street. Lily wrote the names of the shops in her notebook. After ten minutes, Leo stopped and looked at his foot. "My new shoes hurt," he said. "I need a bandage." He walked slowly now. "There is a pharmacy at the corner," said Mia. "It is beside my dad's shop." "Suppose it is closed," said Leo. "It is open until five," said Teacher Kim, "so you have time."

Mia and Lily took Leo to the pharmacy, and May stayed with Teacher Kim. "Follow me," said Mia. "Turn left at the corner, and the pharmacy is on the right." They found it easily, because it had a green sign with a white cross. A woman in a white coat gave Leo a bandage and a small bottle of water. Leo sat on the step and put the bandage on his foot.

When they came out, Lily saw something small and silver on the ground. It was a key, and it lay beside the door of the pharmacy. It had a red ring in the shape of a wheel. Lily picked it up and held it in her hand. "I know this key," said Mia. "It has a wheel ring, and my dad's shop is next door." "Maybe it is lost," said Lily.

They went into the bike shop, and Mia's dad looked up from a bike. "Dad, is this your key?" asked Mia. "Yes, it is!" he said. "I looked for it all morning." Mia hugged her dad. He gave each child a cold drink, and Leo thanked him. Everybody smiled. Later, the club walked back to the bus stop. That evening, Lily wrote a short post for the blog about the key.
